title: Building NOISEEDGE — an AI-powered tool to make crypto trading decisions a little less noisy
author: NoiseEdge
selftext:
We've been working on a side project called NOISEEDGE, and we wanted to share it here and get some honest feedback.

The idea came from a problem we find interesting: crypto markets move fast, there's a lot of information to process, and it can be difficult to turn charts and indicators into a clear trading plan.

So we're building a platform designed to bring some of those tools together:

* 📊 Market charts and technical indicators
* 🤖 An AI assistant that helps explain market conditions and indicator signals
* 🧪 Strategy backtesting to test ideas against historical data
* 🎮 Paper trading and trading competitions, so users can practise without risking real money

Our goal isn't to promise profitable trades or predict every market move. We want to help people analyse, test and learn before making their own decisions.

We're still developing the project, so there's a lot to figure out — especially how to make the experience genuinely useful rather than just adding AI for the sake of it.

We'd love to hear from other builders and traders here:

**What would make a tool like this genuinely useful to you?** Is it better backtesting, clearer explanations of indicators, paper trading, or something else entirely?

Any honest feedback is welcome!

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: with crypto the fill model in the backtester matters more than the AI layer on top. what does a backtest entry assume you paid, the last trade or the ask?

replies.author: NoiseEdge
replies.body: That's a really good point. A backtest is only as realistic as its execution assumptions. We're still developing NOISEEDGE, and getting things like spread, slippage, fees and realistic order fills right is definitely something we need to pay attention to. No point having a great AI layer if the backtest results aren't realistic 😅 Appreciate you bringing this up!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: fees and spread are the easy half to add. the one that bites in crypto is assuming you got filled at all on a thin book when the signal fires into a fast move.

replies.author: NoiseEdge
replies.body: That's a fair point, especially for lower-liquidity pairs. Our main focus is on more liquid markets like BTC, ETH and SOL, where liquidity is generally stronger on major exchanges. Of course, sharp market moves can still cause slippage or execution issues, so it's definitely something worth accounting for. I agree that thin order books are a much bigger concern when dealing with less liquid pairs. Appreciate the technical perspective

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: BTC and ETH on the big exchanges you'll mostly be fine. the slips show up on news candles, so logging the price you asked for next to the price you got from day one tells you fast.
